# The storyboard

The third stop: the script of the whole page, which the person says yes to. Write it to `docs/story/storyboard.md`.

A plan covers what its asker thought to ask for. Most people ask for the idea and for what moves. Nobody asks what the site does on a phone, or without the 3D, or what a shared link shows, and a script that leaves those out is half a script. So this one has a place for each, and an empty place shows.

## The chapters

A row to a chapter:

| Chapter | Its name in the form | The role it holds | What you read | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## The beats

Under each chapter, a row to a beat. A beat is one settled state of the scene and one block of text.

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

- **Screens:** how much scroll the beat takes. One, or more where the scroll works something.
- **How the pieces stand:** a stack, a fan, a ring, a row, a wall, or what the chapter needs. The same pieces in every beat.
- **What is on their faces:** the person's real pictures and words. Name the picture.
- **What the chapter adds:** anything in the scene besides the pieces. Often nothing.
- **Its caption:** a title and a sentence or two, written from the fact sheet.

A caption says nothing the fact sheet does not say. What a project taught the person, what was wrong before they came, how often a thing is used: those are theirs to tell you. Where you want such a sentence and do not have it, write the question in its place.

## Someone with thirty seconds

Say how a visitor who does not scroll gets the name, what the person does, one proof of it, and how to reach them. The first screen carries the first three. A rail jumps to any chapter, and one link skips to the close.

## Without the scene

Say what a visitor gets in each case. The text is ordinary HTML over the scene, so all of it is there in every row. Say what stands in for the pieces.

| Where | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| On a phone | |
| With reduced motion | |
| With no WebGL | |
| With no JavaScript | |

## The look and the type

Both come from the object's material: plates are ceramic on linen, a status page is dark glass, a paper is white with dark ink. Name two or three looks, each as its ground, its ink, one accent, and the surface of the pieces. The person picks by scrolling, once it is built.

Two typefaces: one for the text, and one for what is printed on the pieces, which belongs to the form.

## Everything else the site needs

Mark every row build, later or never, and say who decided.

| | Build, later or never | Who decided |
|---|---|---|
| The way round the page | | |
| A page for each project | | |
| Every project listed | | |
| How to reach them, and a CV | | |

# Storyboard — The Job Card

Concept: [[concepts]], Concept 1. Facts: [[facts]]. Judgement calls: [[decided-for-you]].

The object: eight job cards — simple rounded ticket shapes, like the ones at a bike co-op's counter. One each for: the co-op (2023–present), buying the bike, the inventory, stripping the paint, truing the wheel, the bottom bracket, the hand-crank charger, the pedal box bracket. The same eight cards, rearranged, run from the first screen to the last.

## The chapters

| Chapter | Its name in the form | The role it holds | What you read | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Complaint | The opening — her name, and the question | "Mina Park. Second-year, Mechanical Engineering, Hallam Institute of Technology. Looking for a placement, summer 2026." | Eight cards stand fanned shut, like tickets on a spike | Scroll to begin; a side rail to jump to any chapter; a link straight to Closed out |
| 2 | What I find | Who / Where from — how she works | How she works: SolidWorks, MATLAB, some Python; lathe and mill; the co-op since 2023; a job always starts with what's actually wrong, not what's assumed | Cards loosen into a row, each tilted just enough to show one line — a real diagnosis, in her own words where she gave one | Tap a card to read its line in full |
| 3 | Parts | What — the work laid out | What each job actually was | Cards spread into a wall, flipping to their photo face — the bent wheel, the stripped frame, the seized cup, the scattered garage-floor parts, the charger's housing, the bracket in CAD | Click a card to open it larger; arrow keys move along the wall |
| 4 | What I did | What — the work shown working | What she did on each job | Cards flip again to show the action: redesigned, rebuilt, trued, stripped, freed, sorted | Nothing new — same open/close as chapter 3 |
| 5 | Test ride | What came of it | The outcome of each job, stated plainly, finished or not | Cards flip to their outcome face. Most are closed out; the co-op card stays open, no end date; the bracket's card is marked plainly as not yet run | Nothing new |
| 6 | Closed out | The close — the answer, and how to reach her | The answer to "how do you know what's actually wrong" — you check, and you don't call it fixed until you've tested it; then how to reach her | The eight cards restack into one pile, in order, as at the end of a Saturday | Email link, CV download, a link out to Slow Miles |

## The beats

### Chapter 1 — Complaint

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | 1 | Fanned shut, like a spike of tickets at a counter | Blank ticket fronts, printed header only: "JOB CARD" | Her name and the question, set as if written on the topmost card's header fields | "Mina Park. Second-year, Mechanical Engineering, Hallam Institute of Technology, Sheffield. Looking for a placement, summer 2026. — How do you know what's actually wrong?" |

### Chapter 2 — What I find

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | 1–2, scroll-linked | The fan loosens into a single row | Each card tilts open a crack, showing one handwritten-style diagnosis line: "cracked flange on the hub, hiding under the grease" (wheel); "not the rim" (wheel, alt.); "a seized cup, and the thing I should have checked first" (bottom bracket); "four minutes of cranking for one percent" is withheld here — this chapter shows the finding, not the result | Nothing beyond the row | "What I find. SolidWorks, MATLAB, some Python. A lathe and a mill. Saturdays at Second Gear Bike Co-op since 2023 — where a job starts with what's actually wrong, not what's assumed." |

### Chapter 3 — Parts

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | 1–2, scroll-linked | Row spreads into a wall, roughly 4×2 | Each card flips to its photo: the bike as bought (flat tyre), the garage-floor inventory, the stripped frame, the trued wheel's hub, the bottom bracket cup, the hand-crank charger's gear train and housing, the pedal box bracket in CAD, a plain card for the co-op (text only, no photo) | A loose grid, not a grid line in sight — cards sit at slightly different heights, like tickets actually dropped on a counter | "Eight jobs. One still open." |
| 3.2 | held, no scroll needed | — | Opened detail view of whichever card is clicked | A larger single card, the rest dimmed behind it | Per-card, drawn from facts: e.g. the bracket's card reads "Pedal box mounting bracket, Formula Student chassis sub-team, joined October 2025." |

### Chapter 4 — What I did

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | 1 | Same wall | Cards flip once more to an action line: "Redesigned the mounting bracket," "Rebuilt the gear train and housing," "Trued the wheel," "Stripped forty years of paint," "Freed the seized cup, cleaned it, greased it, put it back," "Laid every part out and sorted it: keep, fix, replace," "Fixed what came in" (co-op, standing in for the many unlisted jobs it covers without a count) | Nothing added | "What I did. Not what I meant to, or what the plan said — what actually happened to each one." |

### Chapter 5 — Test ride

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1 | 1–2, scroll-linked | Wall holds; cards flip to an outcome face | Bracket: "18% lighter — in CAD and in simulation. Not yet machined. Due November 2026." marked with an open, not a tick. Charger: "It worked. Badly: four minutes of cranking for one percent of charge." Wheel: "True again." Bottom bracket: "Back in the frame." Paint: "Stripped to bare steel." Inventory: "Sorted." Bike-as-bought: "The job that opened every ticket after it." Co-op: "Open — every Saturday, since 2023," no closing date | A small open/closed mark on each card, honestly set | "Test ride. A fix isn't one until it's been run. Most of these have; one hasn't yet, and says so." |

### Chapter 6 — Closed out

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6.1 | 1 | Cards restack into a single pile, in order, like a finished day's tickets | Top card only: her email, a CV download, a link to Slow Miles | Nothing else on screen — the pile, and the three links | "That's how you know what's wrong: you check. And you don't call it fixed until you've tested it. — mina@example.com · CV · slowmiles.example" |

Note: every number used above is the one she gave and no other appears — see [[decided-for-you]] for the two that are left out on purpose (the 12th-of-68 result, and "hundreds" of bikes).

## Someone with thirty seconds

The first screen (1.1) carries her name, her field and institute, and the question — that's who she is and what she's after. The fanned eight cards behind the text are the proof at a glance: a visible, countable body of finished and in-progress work, before anyone reads a word of it. A thin side rail, present throughout, jumps straight to any chapter by name; a "Closed out ↓" link in the same rail skips straight to chapter 6, where the email and CV sit. A visitor who never scrolls past screen one still sees the name, the question, and the stack of proof; one click reaches contact.

## Without the scene

| Where | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| On a phone | The same six chapters, same order, same captions. The wall (chapters 3–5) becomes a single vertical column, one card at a time, swiped or tapped through rather than laid out as a wall; the flip is a tap, not a hover. The row in chapter 2 becomes a vertical list. No true 3D or WebGL is used at any point — the cards are flat shapes moved and flipped with CSS — so there's no heavier fallback needed for the phone than a simpler layout of the same pieces. |
| With reduced motion | Every beat appears already in its settled state — fanned, walled, or stacked, whichever that chapter calls for — with no automatic flip or scroll-driven motion. A tap still flips a card open; nothing moves on its own. |
| With no WebGL | No change. The cards are built from flat shapes and CSS, not a 3D engine, so this case does not arise. |
| With no JavaScript | A plain page, top to bottom: heading and question, then each chapter as an ordinary section with its eight cards shown as a simple static grid of image-and-text blocks in their chapter-5 (finished) state, captions as plain paragraphs, the rail as a list of anchor links, and the close as plain text with an email link, a CV link and a link to Slow Miles. Nothing is missing; nothing moves. |

## The look and the type

The object is a job card — a workshop ticket, not a brochure. Three looks, each a plausible one for that object:

1. **Service counter.** Ground: warm kraft/off-white, like ticket card stock (`#F1EAE0`-ish). Ink: near-black charcoal (`#262220`-ish). Accent: a worn safety-orange, like a repair tag's string. Pieces: manila-card surface, a punched hole top-left, a faint perforated edge.
2. **Workshop steel.** Ground: cool brushed-steel grey-blue. Ink: dark graphite. Accent: safety yellow or chain-grease amber. Pieces: look stamped, like a zinc-plated tool tag — slight bevel, no paper grain.
3. **Night ride.** Ground: near-black, like a lane after dark. Ink: warm off-white. Accent: reflective amber, like a bike reflector catching a headlight. Pieces: faintly glow at their edge, as if taped.

Two typefaces: a plain humanist sans for all running text (captions, chapter names, the side rail) — something in the Inter / IBM Plex Sans family, chosen for being read quickly by someone with two minutes, not for personality — and a monospace or typewriter face for everything printed on the cards themselves (the job-card fields, the diagnosis lines, the outcomes), since a real job card is typed or hand-filled, not typeset. IBM Plex Mono or similar.

She picks a look by scrolling through built samples, once this is built — not from the swatches above alone.

## Everything else the site needs

| | Build, later or never | Who decided |
|---|---|---|
| The way round the page | Build — the side rail with chapter jumps and a "Closed out" skip link | Me, from the thirty-second rule |
| A page for each project | Later — once the bracket is actually machined in November 2026, there may be enough for its own page. Not before | Me; worth her confirming nearer the time |
| Every project listed | Build — all eight cards, nothing held back | Me, since nothing in the material needs hiding |
| How to reach them, and a CV | Build — email link and a CV download in chapter 6 | Her, by naming the audience and their two minutes. **Open question for her:** does she have a CV file ready to link, or should the page itself stand in for one for now? |
| What others say | Never | Her — no testimonials exist, and she asked that none be invented |
| Languages | Never — English only | Me; Hallam is a UK institute and nothing in the material suggests otherwise |
| What a shared link shows, and the site's icon | Build — a small favicon (a single job card) and a social-preview image. **Open question for her:** which card or photo should stand in the shared-link preview? | Me to build; her to pick the image |
| The page for an address that is not there | Build — small, styled as a card marked "not found," same look as the rest | Me |
| A blog | Never (here) — Slow Miles already exists; chapter 6 links out to it rather than rebuilding it inside the site | Me; worth confirming she's happy linking out rather than folding posts in |
| A chat | Never | Me — nothing in the material calls for one |
| A legal notice | Never, for now — no data is collected beyond a plain mailto link; revisit if a contact form or analytics is added later | Me |

## What I'm asking for

A yes to this script, or what to change in it. Two things in the table above are genuinely hers to answer when she's ready, not mine to guess: the CV file, and the image for a shared link's preview. Everything else marked "Me" in the "who decided" column is a judgement call she's free to overturn — say which row.

Second-year, Mechanical Engineering, Hallam Institute of Technology, Sheffield. Looking for a placement, summer 2026. — How do you know what's actually wrong?"* One screen. Touch: scroll to begin, or jump anywhere via a side rail.

**2. What I find — who she is, how she works.** The fan loosens into a row; each card tilts open a crack to show one real diagnosis line ("a cracked flange on the hub, hiding under the grease," "a seized cup, and the thing I should have checked first"). Caption: SolidWorks, MATLAB, some Python, a lathe and a mill, Saturdays at the co-op since 2023 — a job starts with what's actually wrong. Touch: tap a card to read its line in full.

**3. Parts — the work laid out.** The row spreads into a loose wall. Cards flip to their photo face: the flat-tyre bike as bought, the garage-floor inventory, the stripped frame, the trued hub, the bottom-bracket cup, the charger's gear train and housing, the pedal box bracket in CAD, and a text-only card for the co-op. Touch: click a card to open it larger; arrow keys move along the wall.

**4. What I did — the work shown working.** Same wall, cards flip to an action line each: redesigned, rebuilt, trued, stripped, freed-cleaned-greased, sorted, fixed-what-came-in.

**5. Test ride — what came of it, stated plainly.** Cards flip to outcome. The bracket reads "18% lighter — in CAD and simulation. Not yet machined. Due November 2026," marked open, not ticked. The charger reads "It worked. Badly: four minutes of cranking for one percent of charge." The co-op card stays open with no closing date. Nothing here is softened or inflated.

**6. Closed out — the close.** All eight cards restack into one pile, in order, like a finished day's tickets. The top card carries her email, a CV download, and a link out to Slow Miles. Caption answers the opening question: *you check, and you don't call it fixed until you've tested it.*

**Thirty-second visitor:** screen one alone gives her name, her field, the question, and eight visible cards as proof at a glance. A rail jumps to any chapter; a "Closed out ↓" link skips straight to contact.

- **Phone:** same six chapters, same captions. The wall becomes one card at a time, swiped through; flips are taps, not hovers. Nothing here ever needed true 3D/WebGL — the cards are flat shapes moved with CSS — so there's no heavier fallback to drop.
- **Reduced motion:** every beat shows its settled end-state directly; nothing moves on its own, a tap still flips a card.
- **No WebGL:** no change — doesn't apply.
- **No JavaScript:** a plain page top to bottom, each chapter an ordinary section, cards as a static grid of image-and-text, rail as a list of anchor links, close as plain text with a mailto link.

## Look and type

Three candidate looks, built as real samples once this is approved and chosen by scrolling, not from swatches alone:
1. **Service counter** — kraft/off-white ground, charcoal ink, worn safety-orange accent, manila ticket surface with a punched hole.
2. **Workshop steel** — brushed steel-grey ground, graphite ink, safety-yellow or grease-amber accent, stamped zinc-tag surface.
3. **Night ride** — near-black ground, warm off-white ink, reflective-amber accent, faintly glowing card edges.

Type: a plain humanist sans (Inter / IBM Plex Sans family) for all running text; a monospace/typewriter face (IBM Plex Mono or similar) for everything printed on the cards themselves, since a real job card is typed or hand-filled, not typeset.

## Everything else the site needs

| | Build / later / never | Decided by |
|---|---|---|
| Way round the page (rail + skip-to-close) | Build | Me |
| A page per project | Later, once the bracket's machined (Nov 2026) | Me — worth confirming nearer the time |
| Every project listed | Build, all eight, nothing hidden | Me |
| Contact + CV | Build | You — but **I need from you:** a CV file to link, or should the page stand in for one? |
| Testimonials | Never | You — none exist, none invented |
| Languages | Never, English only | Me |
| Shared-link preview + favicon | Build | Me to build — but **I need from you:** which photo/card should show in a shared link's preview |
| 404 page | Build, small, same look | Me |
| A blog | Never here — link out to Slow Miles instead of rebuilding it | Me — confirm you're fine linking out |
| Chat | Never | Me |
| Legal notice | Never for now | Me |

Everything marked "Me" is a judgement call, listed in full with reasons in `docs/story/decided-for-you.md` — any of it can be changed, just say which row.

That's the whole script. Say yes and I'll treat the plan as settled (building itself is still a separate step, not part of this), or tell me what to change — including the two things only you can answer: the CV file, and the image for the shared-link preview.
